host: mylinux, Intel i7-14700K, powersave governor unchanged
before: Existing Inkwell/LLVM experiment, captured in before-source.tar.gz; same baseline harness and resident input.
measurements: 4,000,000 rows, batch 8192, windows 1024, nullable input every 17 rows. Three independent process replicas per mode/thread count, each 12 timed samples per case after correctness and two warmups. Report median of per-process medians. Rotated modes; alternating thread-count order. Preparation, kernel prewarm and result destruction outside execute timing.
correctness: 106 existing/new lib and integration tests pass. Every benchmark case validates all output rows, NULLs, duplicate/missing IDs and aggregates against independent Rust calculations before timing; timed samples check row counts.
implementation: Finite scalar/column broadcast shapes are lowered before the row loop for every existing Call signature. No query-expression fusion or constant-value specialization.
Reusable per-LocalState invocation descriptors and output-column list replace per-window heap allocations for generated calls.

GEP pointer arithmetic retains affine memory accesses; exact sign-bit formulas for checked Add/Sub avoid LLVM 19 struct-return intrinsic vectorization barrier. Multiplication still uses its intrinsic.

Last-use analysis recycles owned intermediate columns after their final window read. Output columns remain pinned through all windows. Compatible 64-bit primitive input buffers are borrowed with their Arrow slice offsets and owners.
remaining_limits: Canonical intermediate representation still uses u64 words for narrow values and Booleans. Validity is expanded from Arrow bitmaps and output is reconstructed.
Only scalar Call kernels use the generated library. GroupLookup/AggregateUpdate/Filter have separate vector execution logic; generated/native aggregate timings consequently stay close.
Filtered output still uses selection-vector materialization and Arrow output conversion. No evidence yet that these paths match main.
Four-thread arithmetic/division medians are close to main, with noticeable per-process variability. Do not infer a universal win from single-thread results.
Prewarm latency grows with the number of finite shape variants. Prewarm remains outside query timings and does not imply zero process-start compilation.
ir_evidence: final-add-i64.ll contains vector loops for column/column and both scalar/column shapes, with add <4 x i64> and overflow checks retained. add-i64.ll is the prior struct-return-intrinsic version after GEP; vectorize.log contains compiler diagnostics for that earlier generated module.
